Breakfast at the hotel. At the scheduled time, meet your English-speaking guide in the lobby and set off on a sightseeing tour of Bogotá’s historic centre.

The old quarters retain their colonial churches, narrow streets, squares and architectural landmarks from the 17th to the 19th centuries. Just beyond them is modern Bogotá, with high-rise buildings, cafés, restaurants and shops by local designers. The contrast between old and new is especially apparent as you walk through the centre.

One of the main stops is the Gold Museum, whose collection is devoted to the pre-Columbian era. It includes gold masks, diadems, bracelets, ritual figurines and emblems of authority. Ancient cultures associated gold with the creative energy of the sun, so many of these objects had ritual and symbolic significance.

Next, take the funicular up Monserrate, which stands about 3,200 metres above sea level. The summit offers panoramic views of Bogotá. It is also home to the 17th-century San Vicente monastery, reached by winding stairways.

After Monserrate, continue to the museum dedicated to Fernando Botero, the renowned Colombian painter and sculptor. Lunch at a restaurant is also included in the day’s itinerary.

At the end of the tour, transfer back to the hotel and rest.
Panoramic view of Bogotá, Colombia, with high-rise buildings, roads and mountain slopes
Bogotá: an elevated view of the city’s neighbourhoods, high-rise buildings and roads

Breakfast at the hotel. At the scheduled time, meet your English-speaking guide in the lobby. Today you will leave Bogotá for a full-day trip to Guatavita and Zipaquirá.

The early-morning drive takes you to Lake Guatavita, about 57 km from Bogotá and around 3,100 metres above sea level. It is one of the best-known sites associated with the pre-Columbian legend of El Dorado.

According to the story told on the tour, a ritual marked the accession of a new cacique. The chief went out onto the water naked on a raft and immersed himself in the lake, while his attendants threw gold figurines known as tunjos into the water. This story prompted many attempts over the years to recover the supposed treasures from the lake.

After visiting the lake and learning about its history, continue towards Zipaquirá. The drive takes about an hour and a half.

The main stop is the Catedral de Sal, a cathedral carved entirely out of salt. It lies at a depth of 180 metres below sea level. After visiting the cathedral, you will have time to walk through the town and buy souvenirs.

Lunch at a restaurant. Then return to Bogotá, transfer to the hotel and rest.
